projects.name: Mono-Hydra++
projects.oneLine: The current system. One camera, one IMU, a hierarchical 3D scene graph, and a perception loop that feeds back into state estimation.

repos.name: mono_hydra_vio
repos.role: VIO backend with sparse depth factors

projects.whatItDoes: Predicted sparse depth enters the visual-inertial odometry as metric anchor factors. Semantic masks keep dynamic and unreliable regions out of the estimator. The poses that come back out temporally align the next dense predictions. The loop runs in both directions, which is the whole point.

supporting.caption: Where each learned output enters the estimator. Look at the two return arrows: pose feeds back into perception, not just forward into the map.
The component study. Node F1 and ATE improve under different settings, which is why no single configuration is presented as best.
A failure case: small classes absorbed into neighbouring dominant classes. Shown because the aggregate mIoU hides it.

projects.name: Mono-Hydra
projects.oneLine: Where it started. The first real-time 3D scene graph built from a monocular camera and an IMU.
projects.whatItDoes: Learned depth and learned semantics run as separate networks, feeding a robocentric square-root VIO and the Hydra scene graph layers: mesh, objects, places, rooms, buildings.
keyNumbers: 0.19 m and 0.21 m ITC mean error

projects.name: Learned exploration
projects.oneLine: A deterministic planner proposes only routes it has certified as safe. A learned model chooses among them, or refuses.
projects.statusLabel: Work in progress, no results yet
projects.honesty: The formulation, the layering contract, and the objective are written up in the thesis. The experiments are not run yet, so there are no results to report. The exploration agent does not currently consume the Mono-Hydra++ scene graph either: it maintains its own topological memory over a 2D occupancy map built from simulated depth and pose. Connecting the two acts is the next step.
projects.whatItDoes: The robot enters an unmapped indoor space with one forward-facing camera and must cover it under a time budget without collision. Motion is treated as solved: a geometric planner proposes only routes verified against the occupancy map the robot has built. The open problem is choice, not motion. The learned layer may re-order the certified options and may abstain, but it may never generate a route of its own.
designPoints: Options are judged relative to one another, so that two routes leading through the same opening are not treated as genuine alternatives.
Actions are temporally extended, because passing through a doorway is locally expensive and locally uninformative and everything of value happens afterwards.
Branch memory gives the agent a persistent notion of unfinished work, so regions get completed and exhausted ones get abandoned.
Ensemble disagreement drives abstention, which hands control back to the deterministic layer.
